calibration.note: This is the Multiple Subset-Sum problem (NP-hard by reduction from subset-sum): each payment is atomic and may be applied to at most one invoice, but multiple payments may combine to cover one invoice, so finding a low-cost assignment means partitioning payments into invoice-covering groups. Swept across 20 independently generated scenarios (not just this one): every one of six adversarial greedy probes (spanning every plausible sort-order x accumulation-strategy combination we could construct) landed between 1.5x and 3.3x the exact optimum, with zero exceptions -- this held-out scenario's 2.25x ratio (best_of_six 2696259 vs exact 1196102) is a representative, not favorable, instance. A structurally different reference implementation (simulated annealing local search, independent of the exact bitmask-DP solver) converged to within 0.2-7.0% of the exact optimum across all 20 scenarios (4.8% on this one), confirming the floor is a real property of the problem rather than an artifact of one specific algorithm. The pass bar sits between the local-search reference (1253890) and the best adversarial probe (2696259), close to the reference side, with margin only for legitimate implementation variance.
